items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: This big package was lead by Armando Trovafoli who played piano and I was told that he was the best arranger in Italy.

ctx.x: The next day, we had to give an audition forthe director of the hotel. He started to make a stink because the drummer I had was not the same as the one on a photo that had been sent to him. Felix explained the reason for the change in drummers which I could not understand would make much difference, as long as the rest of us were the same as on the photo. I had gone to all the music shops in Bern long before we had left there and collected as much music as possible, so when we opened in Rome, my band stands were…

The opening was on the 16th of March and we followed a big radio band with singers which was about 25 musicians and singers altogether. This big package was lead by Armando Trovafoli who played piano and I was told that he was the best arranger in Italy. And here I was with my five musicians and one girl singer, trying to please a house that was accustomed to the sound of a big orchestra and a group of singers and accustomed to the sound of comercial music. It was quite a snobbish audience, some women were using…

The next day I taken Felix and "Bass" Hill with me to the American Embassy and we told the lawyer of the Embassy about the affair. He told us that he didn't think there was much we could do and that a contract with anyone in Italy was not worth the paper it was written on, but he would see what he could do. That same afternoon, I received word that we could work an extra day, but the management would not pay our train fare which we had paid from our pockets from Bern to Rome. So we finished on the 19th of March…
